stem.text: A researcher adds a competitive inhibitor to an enzyme-catalyzed reaction and measures kinetics at increasing substrate concentrations. Which change in the enzyme's kinetic parameters is expected?

options.label: A
options.text: The apparent Km increases while Vmax remains unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: Vmax decreases while the apparent Km remains unchanged.

options.label: C
options.text: Both the apparent Km and Vmax increase.

options.label: D
options.text: Both the apparent Km and Vmax decrease.

key_explanation.text: A competitive inhibitor competes with substrate for the active site. At saturating substrate concentrations the substrate outcompetes the inhibitor, so Vmax is unchanged; however, more substrate is required to reach half-maximal velocity, so the apparent Km increases.

strongest_distractor.text: Option B describes pure noncompetitive inhibition, not competitive inhibition: a noncompetitive inhibitor binds a site other than the active site and reduces the effective enzyme concentration, lowering Vmax while leaving Km unchanged.
